rooms.read_aloud:
At the center of the courtyard stands an old stone well, its rim cracked and moss-slick. The darkness inside drinks the light, and cold air spills upward despite the open sky.Beside it, half-buried in rubble, is a stone pedestal. Examining it more closely you can uncover the top is formed into a small bowl with a slot in the bottom. Inside the bowl are the faint outlines of a five pointed star. On opposing sides of the pedestal there are faint relief of what appears to be a king and queenVexatious (father Algren Vayne

“Oooeew—find of the century. Looks just like the one in my father’s garden. There was always money in those. I used to steal it. Fond memories.”

He begins monkeying around with it but steps aside as the party takes alook.DC 10 examination reveals the relief of the king and queenDC15 reveals the secret compartmentDC 15 opens the compartment revealing 18 dirty gold coins with a king and queen on them. pedastal 20 hit pointsIf they put a coin in the slot a faint pulse of blue light emanates from the pedestal and well. For a second the well seems to shimmer, as if it might lead somewhere else.If they put all 18 coins in they can all teleport down to the first level (room 1). Otherwise only 1 person can teleport if they put a coin in and it will take them down into room 1.
rooms.dm_notes:
A small hole in the top of the pedastal is formed into a bowl. There is a slot at the bottom of the bowl. The bowl has a faint five pointed star. On opposing sides are faint relief of king and queen.

DC 10 notice king and queen

DC 15 secret compartment

DC15 open compartment. 18 dirty coins with king and queen

Pedastal 20 hit points. If destroyed, no teleport.

If they place a coin in it, one person can teleport down into room 1. If they place all 18 coins in, the whole party can teleport.

The well: there is a crank. It lowers a large bucket. This does not go down to any water.

Below the ruins is an orc army approaching, so they have to decide quickly.

Vexatious quote included above.

If they choose to go down via well (ladder) they must climb down a slick shaft. DC 10 athletics to avoid slipping. Failure causes 1d6 bludgeoning and loud noise.

If they try to rest on the surface, orcs arrive within 1 hour.

rooms.read_aloud: The guard hall opens into a long, low chamber choked with dust and sagging cobwebs, the air stale with the scent of old rot. Overturned tables lie scattered across the floor, their legs splintered and wood softened by age, as if a final struggle once swept through the room. Beneath the thick gray coating of neglect, careful eyes can make out the shapes of skeletons slumped against walls and tangled beneath benches—some in faded blue tabards, others in red, their rivalry preserved only in scraps of color beneath the grime. At the far end, a broad stone hearth sits cold and blackened. Three figures in blue uniforms huddle before it, seated close as if sharing warmth that no longer exists. One loosely cradles a great axe across his lap. They appear to murmur to each other in voices like dry leaves, as though waiting for an order that never came.
rooms.dm_notes:
Monsters:
4 ghouls  in blue decayed military uniform. One cradles a greataxe, muttering “Wait here…” They animate if disturbed or the axe is moved. While attacking, they repeat “Wait here, wait here.” One zombie never releases the axe, fighting with its free hand and teeth.
Treasure:
Greataxe of Feral Howling: +2 weapon, emits a low growl when drawn. A snarling wolf head is etched into the gleaming metal. Once per day, as a bonus action, you can cause the axe to unleash a supernatural howl in a 30-foot radius. All enemies in range must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or be frightened of you until the end of their next turn.

rooms.read_aloud: The corridor widens into a chamber lined with crumbling stone shelves and shattered map frames. A heavy table dominates the center, its surface scarred by knife marks and burned candle wax. Torn parchment clings to the walls in strips, ink faded to ghosts of battle plans and marching routes. The air here is drier, as if dust has been undisturbed for centuries. In the far corner, a tall wardrobe stands half-open, its door hanging crooked on one hinge. A faint metallic tang lingers, like old blood on iron.
rooms.dm_notes:
The table is covered in old campaign maps. A DC 12 Investigation check reveals a hidden drawer containing:

1) A brass key stamped with a crown-and-flame sigil (opens the stair gate to the lower level).

2) A sealed letter fragment: “Seralith—if the Duke has truly turned, burn the gate and seal the ruby. Do not trust the red banners.”

A DC 10 History/Arcana check connects the sigil to the old royal line.

There is a wardrobe that creaks when opened; inside is a blue officer’s cloak and a cracked signet ring.

If the party spends more than 10 minutes here, distant scraping footsteps echo from the hall.

rooms.read_aloud: Iron bars and narrow stone cells line this cramped hall. Rust flakes from the locks like dried blood, and the smell is sour—mildew, old sweat, and something sharp beneath it. Chains hang from wall rings, some snapped, others still closed as if waiting for wrists that will never return. From the last cell comes a faint shuffling and a wet, eager breathing.
rooms.dm_notes:
Monsters:
The last cell contains a ghoul in red tattered uniform. He’s pacing back and forth in his cell and can be seen from the barred window in the door to the cells. once he notices them he starts dementedly asking them for the keys. “give me the keys” “don’t hide those keys” “give them here” “The duke is coming. “ he’s got the keys!” “ha, he got thirsty”.He’ll rant for awhile and then go back to pacing. If they open the cell he attacks.

There are several skeletons in other cells that animate if the door is opened.

This room includes the key needed to access the lower level if the party didn’t find it elsewhere.

A wight in one cell is shackled and mutters about “the Flame” and “the ruby.” If freed, it tries to flee deeper rather than fight.

Treasure:
A ring of keys (cell keys + one heavy iron key for the stair gate).

rooms.read_aloud: The kitchen is a ruin of broken crockery and collapsed shelves. A long hearth gapes black with soot, and old pots lie scattered like overturned helmets. The air is damp and smells faintly of sour grain. A narrow prep table sits against the wall, its surface scored by knives—and something else: a set of deep gouges, as if claws once raked the wood in frustration.
rooms.dm_notes:
A DC 12 Investigation check turns up a sealed jar of preserved fruit (still edible) and a small silver ladle.

If the party makes loud noise here, a patrol of undead in the adjacent halls is drawn closer.

There are claw marks that hint at something burrowing through the walls.

A patch of pale, ashy growth near the drain suggests cinder-creep mold (if you’re using it).

rooms.read_aloud: The barracks is long and low-ceilinged, the air thick with stale dust that hangs in the beam of any light like drifting ash. Cobwebs stretch in sheets from bunk to bunk. Bedrolls lie half-unfurled as if men rose in a hurry and never returned. In the center, a faded royal tabard—blue stitched with a crowned star—lies folded atop a chest, untouched by rot, as if protected by stubborn memory.
rooms.dm_notes:
Monsters: 3 Skeletons rise from bedrolls.Trap: Touching the royal tabard triggers a falling beam (DC 13 Dex save).Clues:Tabard lining: “From Seralith’s hand. No surrender. No return.”Treasure:Ring of Last Watch: Grants 60 ft. darkvision for 1 hour (1/day).

Monsters:
3 Skeletons rise from bedrolls.
Treasure:
Ring of Last Watch: Grants 60 ft. darkvision for 1 hour (1/day).

rooms.read_aloud: A long hall stretches ahead, its walls draped in banners that once proclaimed loyalties in bright color. Now they hang in tatters—blue and red both, stitched symbols faded and torn. The air stirs strangely here, though there is no breeze. Dust lifts in little spirals along the floor, and the banners whisper against stone as if murmuring names.
rooms.dm_notes:
Some banners bear the crowned-star of Seralith; others the red sigil of the Duke’s faction.

A DC 12 Perception check notices one banner that doesn’t move with the rest—hiding a narrow crack that leads to a concealed niche.

The niche holds a small bundle of letters (handouts) and a bent holy symbol.

If the party lingers, shadows detach from the banner folds and drift closer.

rooms.read_aloud: Rusted weapons line the walls—spears with snapped shafts, swords welded to their scabbards by corrosion, dented shields layered in flakes of iron. A rack of crossbows has collapsed into a heap. The floor is littered with arrowheads and shattered helm-visors. In the center of the room, a single weapon rests on a stand beneath a cracked skylight shaft: a blade too clean for this place.
rooms.dm_notes:
A DC 12 Investigation check confirms most gear is useless, but scavenging yields a handful of serviceable arrows/bolts.

The clean blade is a named relic tied to the demon-prison lore (if you want to seed it here as a clue, not the actual prison-breaking sword).

If removed, a distant clank echoes through the level, as if something answered.

rooms.read_aloud: A small chapel opens off the corridor, its pews splintered and its altar cracked. A mural behind the altar depicts a king and queen beneath a five-pointed star—paint flaking, faces worn by time. The air is colder here, and the silence feels heavy, like a held breath. A faint scent of old incense clings to the stone.
rooms.dm_notes:
A cleric feels a lingering consecration. Turning undead may be unusually effective here, or the altar may grant advantage on a single Channel Divinity effect.

A DC 12 Religion check identifies the star as an old royal-saint symbol tied to Seralith.

A hidden compartment under the altar holds a small vial of holy water and a prayer strip with a warning: “Seal the ruby. The Flame lies.”

rooms.read_aloud: Long tables stretch across the mess hall, half-collapsed and buried in dust. Trencher plates sit where they were left, piled with gray rot. The smell is stale but not foul—more like an old cellar than a grave. A broken chandelier hangs from the ceiling, swaying slightly though nothing moves it. Somewhere in the darkness, a faint clicking repeats at steady intervals.
rooms.dm_notes:
This room is a potential safe-ish rest spot if the party barricades entrances.

The clicking comes from something burrowing in the walls—kruthik activity deeper below.

A DC 12 Investigation check finds a sealed keg with drinkable ale and a pouch with 12 sp.

If the party takes a long rest here without precautions, a wandering undead encounter may occur.

rooms.read_aloud: Tall shelves loom in the darkness, some collapsed into heaps of warped wood and moldy paper. The smell of old parchment is sharp, layered with damp and ash. A reading table sits at the center, its surface strewn with scraps—pages torn, ink smeared, as if someone searched frantically and fled mid-thought. In the far corner, a lectern stands upright, a single book chained to it.
rooms.dm_notes:
The library provides fragments of backstory: Duke Varnholde’s betrayal, Seralith and Aerlan, and the demon’s ruby prison.

The chained book contains three readable fragments (choose or roll):

1) “...the Flame promised victory, but its price was chains.”
2) “Aerlan says the mountain castle is the only place the ruby can sleep.”
3) “Ghurzag dreams in fire. He speaks the Flame’s words.”

If a character spends 10 minutes studying, grant a clue + inspiration or advantage on a future lore check.

Some shelves are infested with pale mold that irritates lungs (Con save DC 12 or cough, giving away position).

rooms.read_aloud: A heavy iron gate blocks a descending stairwell. The metal is cold to the touch and stamped with a crown-and-flame sigil. Beyond the bars, stone steps vanish into blackness. The air rising from below carries a dry heat that feels wrong in this damp ruin—like breath from a distant furnace.
rooms.dm_notes:
This is the lock point to the lower level. It requires the heavy key stamped with crown-and-flame.

Forcing it: DC 18 Athletics. Failure by 5+ makes loud noise and draws an encounter.

If opened, a brief pulse of warmth washes over the party, and faint embers drift up the stairwell before fading.

rooms.read_aloud: The stairs descend into tighter tunnels where the stone changes—older, darker, veined with glittering mineral like trapped starlight. The air is warmer and drier, and the silence is punctuated by occasional faint scratching from somewhere inside the walls. Every so often, you pass a crack that exhales a brief, hot breath, as if the dungeon itself were sleeping and dreaming of fire.
rooms.dm_notes:
This area foreshadows the demon’s influence.

Kruthik tunnels may intersect here.

A DC 12 Perception check spots fresh claw marks and small chitin fragments.

If the party is moving slowly, they may encounter a small scouting group.

rooms.read_aloud: The tunnel opens into a chamber riddled with jagged holes. The floor is littered with shed chitin and pale, broken egg-casings. The air vibrates faintly with a clicking chorus, like impatient teeth. A sour smell clings to the stone—acid and wet earth. Something skitters just beyond the edge of your light.
rooms.dm_notes:
This is a kruthik nest encounter (hatchlings + young as needed).

Terrain: jagged pits and low tunnels grant the kruthik cover and movement advantages.

A DC 12 Nature check identifies acid-scorched stone and warns of burrowing ambush.

Treasure: A half-dissolved adventurer pack in a pit contains 25 gp and a potion (your choice).

rooms.read_aloud: A thick stone door stands ajar, revealing a small vault chamber. The walls are carved with an old royal script, and the floor is inlaid with a five-pointed star motif. Dust lies undisturbed except for a single drag mark leading toward the back wall. In the center, a pedestal sits empty, as if something priceless was removed long ago.
rooms.dm_notes:
The vault is mostly emptied, but it contains lore and a minor magic item.

A DC 13 Investigation check finds a hidden compartment with a sealed scroll tube.

The tube holds a royal decree fragment naming Duke Varnholde and referencing a ‘mountain castle’ and a ‘ruby prison.’

If you want a tangible reward: a charm or minor protective talisman tied to Seralith.

rooms.read_aloud: The tunnel narrows and the stone grows hot beneath your fingertips. Ahead, a fissure splits the wall, exhaling a steady stream of warm air carrying the smell of smoke and something metallic. Fine gray ash coats the floor in drifts, swallowing footprints and muffling sound. Each breath tastes dry, like burnt paper.
rooms.dm_notes:
Environmental hazard: choking ash. Con save DC 12 after 10 minutes or gain one level of exhaustion (or cough loudly, attracting attention).

This is a good place to seed ‘Flame’ whispers: characters hear faint promises in the vent’s hiss.

A DC 12 Survival check can follow ash currents to predict which tunnels connect deeper.

rooms.read_aloud: Carved stone pillars frame this circular chamber. The floor is etched with concentric rings of runes, and at the far side stands a sealed doorway of black basalt, its surface veined with red lines that pulse faintly like a heartbeat. The air hums with restrained power. A whisper coils at the edge of hearing—soft, intimate, and hungry.
rooms.dm_notes:
This chamber is a lore-heavy threshold to the demon prison story.

The runes are a ward. A DC 14 Arcana check reveals the seal is meant to contain something.

If disturbed, the ward lashes out (minor psychic/radiant backlash, your choice).

The party should leave with the sense that Fort Aelwind is only a hint of a larger, hidden war.

rooms.read_aloud: The passage slopes upward, the air gradually cooling and dampening. Roots push through cracks overhead, and the stone changes from ancient black to the familiar gray of the fort’s foundations. Ahead, you can smell rain and fresh earth—an exit to the wilds beyond the ruins. Behind you, the dungeon’s warm breath fades, but the memory of its whispers lingers.
rooms.dm_notes:
This tunnel provides an alternate exit to avoid the surface orc army.

It can also serve as a pursuit route for enemies.

If the party leaves without dealing with key threats, foreshadow consequences: the Flame’s influence spreads; Ghurzag’s forces tighten their net.

npcs.name: Vexatious Wayne
npcs.appearance: A sharp-eyed, well-dressed boy with mud on his boots and a perpetual smirk.
npcs.personality: Smart but not wise; curious, impulsive, delighted by danger and treasure.
npcs.voice: Fast, bright, a little nasal; talks as if everything is a joke he’s already in on.
goals: Impress adults while pretending he doesn’t care
Get one over on his father, Algren Vayne

relationships.name: Algren Vayne
relationships.notes: City councilor; Vexatious tries to provoke and outshine him.

statblock.notes: Use Commoner stats with Dex 14, Int 12; HP 6; Speed 30; Dagger +4 to hit, 1d4+2 piercing.

features: Nimble Escape (1/turn): Disengage or Hide as a bonus action.
actions: Dagger. Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 1d4+2 piercing.
npcs.tactics: Avoids direct fights; hides, distracts, and shouts unhelpful ‘advice’.
secrets_and_hooks: Knows rumors about hidden compartments and old coins with the king/queen stamp.
May have stolen something important from his father without realizing it.
npcs.dm_notes: Use him to point at obvious interactables (well, pedestal) and to inject humor or urgency.
